points: Q3 2026 results will show whether the 7% year-over-year revenue growth and raised full-year guidance from Q2 are carrying into the back half; a continuation supports the long case.
The 8-up/0-down analyst revision skew over the past 30 days and the +0.57% 90-day revenue estimate revision point to upward estimate momentum; Q3 needs to validate that optimism.
Consensus FY1/FY2 EPS growth is only ~3.4% and ~3.1%, so the print must confirm that an ~11.3x forward P/E is backed by stable earnings; any guidance lift would improve the elevated PEG ratio.

NorthStar 2030 execution and new program awards/bookings are the forward drivers; reports suggest the strategy gained traction in Q2, and Q3 commentary should show whether that pipeline is converting.
Peer prints from WWD on Oct. 29 and MOG-A on Nov. 1 will provide sector read-throughs on aerospace/defense demand and margins right before LDOS reports; strength there would reinforce the long setup.

The mixed valuation flag — P/E at 0.3x theme median but PEG at 3.1x theme median — means the stock looks cheap on earnings but priced for slow growth; Q3 needs to show earnings can grow into that low P/E or the PEG premium will be questioned.
Updates to full-year 2026 guidance and any color on 2027 budget visibility will determine whether the FY2 ~3.1% EPS growth estimate can be maintained or revised higher.
watch: Revenue growth year-over-year at or above the Q2 7% pace — supports the long
Backlog/bookings growth or major new program awards — supports the long
Operating margin expansion or stable margin execution — supports the long
Full-year 2026 EPS guidance raised or maintained with confident commentary — supports the long
